yt_description:
Dive into the world of graph algorithms with our unique visualization of Depth-First Search (DFS) implemented on a map of Singapore's iconic Marina Bay. Utilizing a captivating magma neon color palette, this video breaks down the DFS algorithm in an intuitive and visually engaging way.

What is DFS?
Depth-First Search is a fundamental algorithm for traversing or searching tree or graph data structures. It starts at an arbitrary node and explores as far as possible along each branch before it backtracks. Think of it as a meticulous explorer who follows a single path to its end, and only then returns to explore alternative paths from previous decision points.

In this visualization, you'll witness:
- How DFS systematically explores the interconnected streets of Marina Bay.
- The process of visiting nodes and edges.
- The backtracking mechanism when a path reaches a dead end or is fully explored.
- A practical application of a core computer science concept.

Perfect for students learning about data structures and algorithms, developers looking for a refresher, or anyone interested in the visual representation of computational processes. Learn DFS not just from theory, but by seeing it in action on a real-world map!
